layout_dets.text: A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Yifan Shi1,2, Wei Zhang1, Tianyi Cui²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1Peking University 2DeepSeek-AI

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Modern software—from plugin systems to self-evolving agent harnesses—increasingly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires dynamic composition, yet its formal foundations remain underdeveloped. We identify

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two orthogonal dimensions of the problem: temporal composability, the ability to completely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revert a component's side effects upon removal, and spatial composability, the ability to declare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and reactively manage inter-component dependencies. We address the two dimensions by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lifting classical effect and coeffect concepts to runtime mechanisms. In particular, we formalize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revertible effects, in which every context transformation carries an inverse that the runtime holds,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: establishing temporal composability local to one component. We formalize reactive coeffects, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which every context change is classified against a component's coeffect specification to drive its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activation and deactivation, establishing spatial composability local to one component. We then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unify the effect context and the coeffect context into a single context type and mediate every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect and coeffect through it, yielding a discipline we call the context paradigm; the mediation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: induces an observational equivalence up to which the effects of distinct components interleave

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without disturbing one another. Combining these mechanisms into the notion of a component,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we give a calculus of dynamic composition whose metatheory carries spatiotemporal compos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability from a single component to a whole system of interleaved components. We implement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these ideas in Cordis, a meta-framework of spatiotemporal composability that provides a core

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: library with effect tracking and coeffect resolution, as well as a declarative component loader

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with configuration reconciliation and hot module replacement.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Composition—assembling complex systems from simpler parts—is a foundational principle of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: software engineering [1]. Traditionally, composition is static: function calls, module imports,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and class inheritance are resolved at compile time and remain fixed throughout execution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, modern software increasingly demands dynamic composition, where components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are loaded, unloaded, and reconfigured at runtime. Plugin architectures [2] and self-evolving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agent harnesses both require systems that can safely add and remove functionality on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fly, yet current practice defers to coarse-grained mechanisms [3] that reconfigure only by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restarting, discarding runtime state. Despite the growing practical importance of dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition, its theoretical foundations remain underdeveloped, compared to the rich formal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frameworks available for static composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.1. Dimensions of Composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To characterize the requirements of dynamic composition, we identify two orthogonal dimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sions beyond the well-studied algebraic aspects of composition:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Temporal composability addresses the time dimension: upon removal of a component,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the modifications the component made to the shared environment must be completely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and safely reversed. This requires tracking every resource allocation, event registration,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and state mutation the component performs, and guaranteeing their orderly reclamation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: upon removal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Spatial composability addresses the space dimension: components must be able to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declare, discover, and resolve their dependencies on one another in a structured and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: verifiable manner. This requires managing dependency topology and coordinating com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ponent lifecycles in response to dependency changes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the static setting, temporal composability reduces to lexical scoping (e.g., RAII [4],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bracket patterns [5]), and spatial composability reduces to module import resolution [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the dynamic setting, where components arrive and depart at runtime, both dimensions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: become significantly harder: temporal composability must handle long-lived, stateful effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose scope is not lexically bounded; and spatial composability must handle dependencies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that appear, disappear, or change identity during execution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.2. Motivating Examples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.2.1. Plugin Systems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Plugin systems are a canonical instance of dynamic composition. We use Visual Studio Code

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (VSCode), one of the most widely-used extensible IDEs, as a representative example.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal limitation. VSCode runs all extensions in a shared process called the extension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: host. Although extensions can be installed dynamically, this host provides no mechanism to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unload an individual extension's code at runtime. Once an extension's activate function has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: executed, disabling or uninstalling it requires restarting the entire host, affecting all loaded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extensions. Purely declarative extensions such as themes, keybindings, and snippets carry no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: code and can be removed freely. Among the top 100 extensions by install count, however, 87

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contain executable code¹ and will therefore require such a restart upon removal. Although

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: VSCode provides a deactivate hook, it serves only as a graceful shutdown callback during the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: host process' termination, and thus does not enable live removal. Moreover, the hook separates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect disposal from effect creation (in activate), violating locality of concern and making

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complete cleanup difficult to verify.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial limitation. VSCode does provide extensionDependencies for declaring dependen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cies between extensions, but it sees little use: among the top 100 extensions by install count,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only 7 declare extensionDependencies on non-built-in extensions. This scarcity reflects the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape of the extension API, which exposes fixed, surface-level extension points such as com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mands, views, and language features. Extensions contribute to the host through these points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rather than depending on one another, so inter-extension dependencies rarely arise. Moreover,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: VSCode's mechanism for inter-extension interaction provides no structural contract: it exposes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an extension's functionality to others through vscode.extensions.getExtension(...) .exports,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but the returned value is untyped (any by default), so the dependent cannot rely on a checked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface. In short, VSCode steers extensions toward a fixed set of host-provided extension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points, and offers no safe, structured way for them to depend on one another.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These two limitations are not unique to VSCode; they recur across plugin systems generally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [2, 7], differing only in degree.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.2.2. Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Modern AI agents rely on runtime agent harnesses [8–10]. These systems may compose diverse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tool suites [11] and execution environments, govern permissions and sandboxing, maintain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: session state and persistence, provide context management and memory systems [12], orches-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trate subagents and multi-agent workflows [13], and expose interfaces to users and automation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A future harness may generate and deploy modifications to its own components while contin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uously serving requests. Model-synthesized reusable tools provide a narrower precursor to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component-level self-modification [14]. Each such modification is itself an instance of dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Because these modifications occur continuously and with limited or no human oversight,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamic composability becomes indispensable. Without temporal composability, each self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modification forces a full restart that discards all process-local accumulated state; at such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequency the cumulative unavailability becomes substantial, and in-flight tasks are disrupted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repeatedly; even worse, a faulty self-modification can disable the very process needed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recover. Without spatial composability, each module must itself detect and adapt to changes in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the modules it depends on as they appear, disappear, or change identity, and can do so only by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ad hoc means; even worse, a naive code-replacement strategy may silently break dependents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or introduce circular dependencies that surface only at reload time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.2.3. The Coarse-Grained Workaround

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One reason dynamic composability has received limited formal attention is that operating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systems and container orchestrators already provide a coarse-grained substitute. Operating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systems yield temporal composability at the granularity of a process; container orchestrators

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1Data retrieved from the Visual Studio Code Marketplace on June 9, 2026.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [3] yield spatial composability at the granularity of a service. In practice, most software toler-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ates the lack of fine-grained composability by deferring to these coarse-grained mechanisms:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a misbehaving module is handled by restarting the process, and a service dependency is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: managed by the container orchestrator.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, this workaround imposes substantial costs. Temporally, each restart discards all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process-local accumulated state (e.g., caches, connections, partial computations), and rebuild-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing it takes seconds to minutes [15]; maintaining availability in the interim requires redundant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replicas, incurring resource overhead to compensate for the inability to recover a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component. Spatially, container-level orchestration cannot express dependencies between com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ponents sharing an address space, and introduces network overhead for interactions that could

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be local function calls. Both mechanisms operate at the boundary of processes and containers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet modern systems increasingly compose at a finer level. This granularity mismatch demands

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a compositional abstraction that manages effects and dependencies at the same level as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components themselves.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.3. Contributions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The two dimensions of dynamic composability concern, respectively, how computations modify

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and how they depend on their environment. These two directions are what effect systems [16,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 17] and coeffect systems [18, 19] formalize: effects provide the formal vocabulary for reasoning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about environmental modifications, and coeffects for reasoning about environmental require-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments. However, existing formulations restrict reasoning to compile-time analysis over lexically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fixed scopes, and do not extend to dynamic scenarios where components arrive and depart at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runtime. By lifting effects to a revertible runtime model and coeffects to a reactive dependency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution mechanism, we obtain a unified formal foundation for dynamic composability,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one that is language-agnostic and applicable to any software architecture requiring dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition. We make the following contributions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. We formalize revertible effects (Section 3.1): every context transformation carries an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explicit inverse that the runtime holds, and both tracking and recovery preserve com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position, so the context is recovered upon component removal. This establishes local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temporal composability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. We formalize reactive coeffects (Section 3.2): a component declares the coeffects it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires as a specification, and each change of the context is classified against that speci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fication as activating, deactivating, or neutral, driving the component's activation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deactivation. This establishes local spatial composability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. We introduce the context paradigm (Section 3.3): the effect context and the coeffect con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: text are unified into a single context type, every effect and coeffect is mediated through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it, and the mediation induces an observational equivalence up to which the effects of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinct components attain independence.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. We develop a calculus of dynamic composition (Section 4), which combines the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanisms into the notion of a component and gives them an operational semantics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The metatheory then carries spatiotemporal composability from a single component to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a whole system of interleaved components.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. We implement these ideas in Cordis (Section 5), a meta-framework of spatiotemporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composability that provides a core library realizing the formal model with effect tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and coeffect resolution, as well as a declarative component loader with configuration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconciliation and hot module replacement.

layout_dets.text: 2. Preliminaries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This section provides a concise overview of effect and coeffect systems—the two theoretical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pillars underlying our work. We assume familiarity with basic type theory and category

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theory; the goal here is to fix notation and introduce the key abstractions that Section 3 will

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operationalize as runtime mechanisms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the simply typed lambda calculus (STLC) [20, 21], a typing judgment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: states that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: term t has type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under context Γ. An effect system refines the type to describe what side effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a computation may produce, yielding judgments of the form

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Here, the result type is annotated with an element of an effect algebra that describes which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: side effects the computation may produce, enabling compositional reasoning about stateful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3. Relationship to Dynamic Composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect and coeffect systems organize reasoning about computation along two complementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directions: effects describe how a computation modifies its environment, whereas coeffects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: describe how it depends on its environment. These two directions correspond to the two dimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sions of dynamic composability identified in Section 1:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Temporal composability demands that a component's modifications to the shared envi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ronment be revertible upon unloading. The relevant effects are the stateful ones, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: durably transform that environment; undoing such a transformation requires it to admit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an inverse.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Spatial composability demands that inter-component dependencies be declared and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: managed reactively. Such dependencies are the very thing coeffects capture, and manag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing them amounts to resolving each against what the environment supplies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, classical effect and coeffect systems are static instruments: effects are tracked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within lexically fixed scopes and discharged by compile-time handlers; coeffect annotations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are verified against contexts determined before execution. Dynamic composition, by contrast,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires these guarantees to hold for components that arrive and depart at runtime, against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contexts that evolve continuously. No fixed lexical scope can delimit a plugin loaded after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deployment; no compile-time context can anticipate dependencies that emerge from runtime

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: configuration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This motivates a shift in perspective: rather than extending static type systems with more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations, we reify the conceptual structures of effects and coeffects so that a runtime can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operate on them directly, establishing dynamically the guarantees these systems provide stat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ically.

layout_dets.text: 3. Revertible Effects and Reactive Coeffects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This section lifts the concepts of effects and coeffects introduced in Section 2 to runtime

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanisms, constructing a theory of dynamic composition. The central idea is to turn the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typing contexts carrying effects and coeffects into context types, runtime-operable types that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reify the context as a first-class entity. Section 3.1 models an effect as a context transformation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paired with an inverse that the runtime holds, establishing temporal composability local to one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component; Section 3.2 models a coeffect as a declared dependency against which every context

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change is classified, establishing its spatial counterpart. Each local guarantee stops where other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components enter. Toward the global form of both, Section 3.3 unifies the two contexts into one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and introduces the context paradigm: every effect and coeffect is mediated through the unified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context, and the mediation induces the observational equivalence up to which every later

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equality is read. Section 3.4 then establishes effect independence and coeffect commutativity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under which the effects of distinct components interleave without disturbing one another.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Revertible Effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal composability is the ability to load and unload components at runtime such that, upon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unloading, the shared environment is recovered to its pre-composition state. This requires that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: every modification a component makes to the environment be both trackable and recoverable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We therefore model an effect as a function of type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trackable. We call such effects revertible: by composing these inverses during execution, local

layout_dets.text: temporal composability becomes a structural guarantee.
